Opensidian 0.9.4 is a feature and bug-fix release on top of 0.9.3. The downloads are the same as 0.9.3 (two AppImages, Flatpak, RPM, DEB) for Linux x86_64.

Every file below has a GitHub artifact attestation (SLSA build provenance) proving it was built by this repository's `release.yml` workflow on GitHub-hosted runners.

**This is a draft. SHA256SUMS is not GPG-signed yet.** The maintainer signs it offline before the release is published.

**The RPM is not signed.** No RPM signing key is used in CI. Check the RPM like every other file: with `SHA256SUMS` and `gh attestation verify` (see Verification).

## Features

### Obsidian theme compatibility (#59)
- Callouts: `> [!type]`, `> [!type]+` and `> [!type]-` with an optional title render like Obsidian in reading view and Live Preview, so themes and CSS snippets style them. (PR #82)
- Panes and tabs carry Obsidian's classes, and themes can set tab and heading colours. (PR #84)
- Many more stock Obsidian CSS variables are defined and used, so a theme restyles much more of Opensidian. With no theme loaded, nothing changes. (PR #85)
- The app's dialogs carry Obsidian's dialog classes. (PR #86)
- Under a chosen theme, the tab strip and the active tab's title colour follow the theme the way Obsidian does. (PR #93)

### Editor
- The editor has a right-click menu (clipboard, Format, Paragraph, Insert, Add link; plugin items come after the built-in ones), and tables render in Live Preview with their own table menu. A right-click never follows or creates a wikilink. (#37, PR #88)

### Bookmarks
- You can bookmark the global graph (with its settings), a local graph, a canvas, and plugin boards such as Excalidraw, from the tab menu or by dragging the tab onto Bookmarks. Bookmarks are saved in Obsidian's `bookmarks.json` format, so they work in both apps. (#31, PR #89)

### Plugins and security
- The dialog shown when a plugin starts a program has a third choice, **Always allow this program**. The grant only applies while the vault, the plugin and the program file are all unchanged; if the plugin or the program changes, you are asked again. Deny stays the default. (#74, PR #77)

## Fixes
- PDFs: pages are drawn on white paper. Before, most PDFs showed as an empty dark pane in 0.9.3. (#44, PR #78)
- Dragging an Excalidraw board's tab onto Bookmarks bookmarks it. (#48, PR #76)
- The caret is visible on an empty task row (`- [ ] `), and text typed there goes into the task. (#75, PR #80)
- Excalidraw drawings (and other web content) only appeared after you interacted with them on X11 without a compositor. Opensidian now turns off WebKitGTK's DMA-BUF renderer only there. Wayland and composited X11 keep it on, and an explicit `WEBKIT_DISABLE_DMABUF_RENDERER` is respected. (#79, PR #87)
- Live Preview: a callout heading is only drawn on the first line of a quote. (PR #90)
- Menus: a menu rebuilt in place is kept inside the window. (PR #91)
- Dialogs: `.modal-container` is only present while an app dialog is open. (PR #92)

### Packaging and build
- The release workflow keeps the release's tag and target when it re-runs on an existing draft. Before, a re-run could leave the draft as `untagged-…`.
- The Flatpak metadata lists the 0.9.4 release.

## Known issues
- Choosing the default theme by name paints the tab strip differently from having no theme set. (#96)
- A 38 px difference on the Solarized route in the built-in theme checks. This was already there before 0.9.4.
- The obsidian-git diff view differs from Obsidian in one compatibility check. This was already there before 0.9.4.
- The DMA-BUF fallback (#87) only applies on X11 without a compositor. Wayland has not been tested with it.

## Verification
Download every file of this release into one directory, then:

```sh
# 1. checksums: every file must report OK
sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS

# 2. build provenance: each file was built by this repository's
#    release workflow on GitHub Actions
for f in opensidian-0.9.4-x86_64* SHA256SUMS; do
  gh attestation verify "$f" -R jpzk/opensidian
done
```

The RPM is unsigned, so `rpm -K` reports no signature. Use the two checks above for it.

**Still to come:** the maintainer's GPG signature of SHA256SUMS (`SHA256SUMS.asc`). It is added before this draft is published. Once it is there, check it with `gpg --verify SHA256SUMS.asc SHA256SUMS`.
